source:
Create a highly addictive Roblox game called "SATISFYING FACTORY".

The game should be inspired by modern viral Roblox games with simple gameplay loops, satisfying animations, colorful visuals, funny sounds, progression, collecting and extremely satisfying interactions.

The main concept:

Each player owns a small factory.

Players collect basic objects from the map and bring them into their factory.

Inside the factory, machines automatically process the objects.

The entire processing system must feel extremely satisfying.

For example:

- Objects fall onto conveyor belts.
- Objects bounce, rotate and roll.
- Machines crush objects.
- Objects get cut into pieces.
- Objects get melted.
- Objects get compressed.
- Objects get transformed into better objects.
- Finished objects come out of the machines with satisfying sounds and particle effects.
- Coins pop out when objects are successfully processed.

Make the animations smooth and satisfying.

Add strong visual feedback:

- Coins flying toward the player
- Numbers appearing when money is earned
- Objects changing color
- Glow effects
- Sparks
- Small explosions
- Screen shake
- Combo effects
- Pop-up notifications
- Satisfying sound effects

GAMEPLAY LOOP:

1. Collect objects.
2. Put them into the factory.
3. Watch the machines process them.
4. Earn money.
5. Upgrade machines.
6. Unlock better objects.
7. Expand the factory.
8. Automate production.
9. Discover extremely rare objects.
10. Repeat and become the richest factory owner.

OBJECT RARITIES:

Common
Uncommon
Rare
Epic
Legendary
Mythic
Secret
Impossible

Examples of objects:

Apple
Toy
Rock
Glass
Diamond
Gold
Robot
Alien Crystal
Meteor
Black Hole
Rainbow Cube
Galaxy Core
Secret Mystery Object

FACTORY MACHINES:

Crusher
Cutter
Melter
Press
Laser
Recycler
Duplicator
Rainbow Machine
Galaxy Machine
Secret Machine

Each machine should have increasingly satisfying animations and effects.

UPGRADES:

Players can upgrade:

- Processing speed
- Machine power
- Conveyor speed
- Storage capacity
- Coin multiplier
- Critical processing chance
- Rare object chance
- Factory size

Add a prestige system called RESTART.

When players reach a very high factory level, they can restart their factory and receive permanent bonuses.

Add pets that follow the player and provide bonuses.

Pet rarities:

Common
Rare
Epic
Legendary
Mythic
Secret

Add eggs that players can open to obtain pets.

Add a large colorful world with several factory areas:

Starter Factory
Candy Factory
Toy Factory
Technology Factory
Volcano Factory
Space Factory
Galaxy Factory
Secret Factory

Each new area introduces new objects, machines and visual effects.

GLOBAL EVENTS:

Every few minutes, trigger a random server-wide event.

Examples:

MEGA OBJECT EVENT:
A gigantic object appears and every player can help process it.

GOLDEN RAIN:
Thousands of golden objects fall from the sky.

SUPER SPEED:
All machines become 10x faster for 30 seconds.

RAINBOW EVENT:
All objects temporarily become rainbow objects.

BLACK HOLE:
A black hole appears and starts sucking objects from the map.

SECRET OBJECT:
A mysterious object appears somewhere in the world and only one player can find it.

Add a collection book where players can discover and collect every object in the game.

Add a global leaderboard showing:

Richest Player
Highest Factory Level
Most Objects Processed
Most Secret Objects Found
Longest Play Time

Make the game extremely easy to understand within the first 10 seconds.

The player should immediately see:
COLLECT → PROCESS → EARN → UPGRADE → REPEAT.

Make the game colorful, polished, funny and highly satisfying.

Use smooth Roblox animations, excellent sound design, particles, physics-based object movement, screen effects and satisfying UI feedback.

The game should be optimized for mobile, tablet and PC.

Make the interface simple and modern.

The first 5 minutes should be extremely rewarding so new players immediately understand the progression and want to continue playing.

Add many small satisfying interactions throughout the game so that almost every action produces visual or audio feedback.

The goal is to create a Roblox game that feels extremely satisfying to watch and play, and that can generate viral YouTube Shorts and TikTok clips.

IMPORTANT:
Do not make the game complicated at the beginning. Start with one simple factory and gradually introduce new mechanics, machines, objects, pets, areas and events as the player progresses.

answers.ask: How big is one factory plot at full expansion, and are the eight areas one continuous world or separate places?
answers.answer: Use a compact factory plot that expands to roughly a 60x60-stud footprint at full expansion, enough for a clear automated production line without becoming overwhelming. Make the eight factory areas separate themed zones within one continuous world, unlocked in progression order.

answers.ask: Is the collecting ground shared by the whole server, or does each player have their own patch?
answers.answer: Use a shared collecting ground in each world area so players can see one another collecting and compete for rare spawns. Keep object respawns frequent so the shared space stays rewarding for everyone.

scene_prompt: Create a colorful 3D factory-world map with eight separate themed zones connected in one continuous progression path: Starter, Candy, Toy, Technology, Volcano, Space, Galaxy, and Secret Factory areas. Each zone has a shared collecting ground where basic and rare objects spawn, with visible routes leading to individual player-owned factory plots. Each factory plot begins small and expands to roughly a 60x60-stud footprint, organized as a clear automated production line: object intake at the front, conveyor belts carrying objects through crusher, cutter, melter, press, laser, recycler, duplicator, rainbow, galaxy, and secret machines, then finished-object outputs at the back. Use open sightlines so players immediately see the collect-to-factory flow, with animated belts, processing chambers, storage areas, and space for expanding machinery. Include a central shared-event space in the world with enough open sky and ground for oversized falling objects, golden-object rain, rainbow effects, or a large black-hole landmark.
blob:
### Genre
Simulation is dominant: this is a factory-management and collection loop with player-owned production space. No secondary genre is needed.

### Shape and preset
Use `world-open`, a single continuous shared factory world where themed collecting grounds and private factory plots coexist along one progression route. This takes the Simulation shape from the Incremental Simulator preset, but the preset is none because its bazaar and generic purchase-gate bundle are not the scene’s defining layout.

### Config requirements
Use `resource-shared` for one shared object-collecting ground in each themed area, visibly open to all players. Use `path-circulation` for clear, broad routes linking every collecting ground, factory-plot frontage, and the event space. Use `gate-progression` for readable thresholds between the eight sequential themed zones. Use `trigger-task` for each plot’s visible front intake and production interaction points. Use `collectible-nodes` for the objects visibly scattered and respawning across shared grounds.

### Layout requirements
Place `collectible-nodes` across all eight shared collecting grounds, with frequent spawn positions distributed over each zone rather than concentrated at a single point. Place `trigger-task` at the front intake of every individual factory plot and along machine interaction points in its production line. No additional placed gameplay volumes are required.

### Layout components
Build eight consecutive themed zones in this exact order: Starter, Candy, Toy, Technology, Volcano, Space, Galaxy, and Secret Factory. Each zone contains a central shared collecting ground, individual player-owned plots reached by short visible access routes, and a clear threshold onward to the next zone. Arrange plots as expandable rectangular factory pads, each reaching roughly a 60x60-stud footprint at full expansion. Within every plot, run the production line front to back: object intake, animated conveyor belts, crusher, cutter, melter, press, laser, recycler, duplicator, rainbow machine, galaxy machine, secret machine, then rear finished-object outputs and storage. Leave lateral expansion bays for added machinery. Put a large central shared-event plaza near the world midpoint, with open ground and unobstructed sky for oversized objects, golden-object rain, rainbow effects, and a black-hole landmark. Keep sightlines open from collecting grounds to plots. Enclose the outer map with themed natural or architectural perimeter barriers while keeping all eight zones on one contiguous surface. Compose the world as a long, highly readable progression spine, with colorful factory silhouettes and the event plaza as the central visual anchor.

### Render order
Use `topdown` first and make it authoritative, because the continuous route, ordered zone thresholds, shared grounds, and plot access must remain connected and legible for play.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is huge, driven by eight full themed zones, a central event plaza, shared collection grounds, and many expandable player plots. Theme: colorful, polished, toy-like viral factory spectacle with exaggerated machinery, glowing processing effects, and clear readable flow. Pipeline modifier `P0`: the world remains one contiguous ground-level surface with no forced overhangs, interior transitions, separate maps, or volumetric traversal.
